ENCLUSURE 2
REPORT ON TRANSPLANTING RARE PLANTS FROM THE BAD CREEK AREA
In 1973 Duke Power Company asked Dr. C. Leland Rodgers, Professor of Botany at Furman University, to conduct a botanical survey of the proposed Bad Creek Pumped-Storage Hydroelectric site in Oconee County, South Carolina. Dr. Rodgers was assisted in the work by Mr. Joseph Green, a botany student at Furman.
During the field work five plant species rarely found in South Carolina were located. The researchers recommended to Duke that individuals of these species be transplanted to similar nearby habitats to help insure their survival. Duke agreed that this work should be done. In the summer of 1974 Dr. Rodgers, with help from Duke-biologists, transplanted the following species:
Species
Number Transplanted
Ginseng (Panax quinquefolium)
38
American Climbing Fern (Lygodium passatum)
21
Wintergree (Gaultheria procumbens)
Several hundred
Witch-alder (Fothergilla major)
26
Lysimachia fraseri
22
In May 1975 the transplanted individuals were inspected and found to be thriving in their new locations
